title: Bound Ask your book's statement reads to what is drawn
body:
## Summary
Answering a question in Ask your book reads deal_evidence for every deal in the answer: 500 reads for 9 drawn rows on the large world.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/book/Ask.tsx:61-62 passes every row of the answer to useEvidenceOf, so a question that names no time ("Who decided: my rules or me?") reads the PayPal evidence of every deal on record. apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/book/evidence.ts:1-7 states the rule this breaks ("Only what is drawn is read", scale finding #17), which the ledger and the meter keep. While those reads are out, Ask.tsx:59-65 counts every unread row as statement 'unknown', whose tip (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/model.ts STATEMENT_TIP.unknown) says "could not be read": a load reported as a failure. Fixed: read statements only for the reconciliation view (bounded by captures) or only for rows in view, and show the pivot's statement column only where it was read; an unread statement is a quiet dash, never "unknown".

## Flow
- open Book > Ask your book on ?scale=large
- tap "Who decided: my rules or me?" then Show answer
- Ask.tsx:62 useEvidenceOf(500 ids) -> 500 deal_evidence calls through the READ_CONCURRENCY gate
- pivot statement column shows "N unknown" chips until they land

## Expected impact
The owner's Ask answers stop issuing hundreds of IPC reads per question and stop calling unread statements unreadable; measured by the read budget in the smoke harness. Could break: the statement column for deal views if it is dropped.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - deal_evidence reads per answered question bounded by rows drawn
Before: probe (large world, "decided" lens): deal_evidence 0 -> 500 after Show answer, 9 rows in the DOM, 500 deals on record
After: predicted <= rows drawn (+ the capture set for the reconciliation view); not built: the statement column's content is a UX choice
Method: probe - book.test-style harness run counting r.budget.byCommand.get('deal_evidence'); the fix was not built because it changes what the pivot shows
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: book.test.tsx: render #m=book&v=ask at large, run the "decided" question, assert budget deal_evidence <= rows drawn; seed by reverting and watch 500

title: Make the window's and the wallet's "by day" lines use one calendar
body:
## Summary
Ask's two tables group "by day" differently: the window by the owner's local day, the wallet by the UTC day, so 37 of 500 large-world deals sit on different days in the two tables (UTC+2).

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/model.ts:111-115 dayKey uses local getDate(); crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:56 groups by date(created_at,'unixepoch') (UTC). Ask.tsx shows both tables for one question (Pivot and WalletAnswer), and the CSV day column uses the local key. Typed ranges are already worked out in the owner's calendar (understand.ts whenSpan), so the wallet's grouping is the odd one out. Fixed: the BookQuery carries the owner's UTC offset (or the client groups by the wallet's UTC day and says so); either is an in-tree contract change (table-core BookQuery, bindings, mock backend) with a verifier to write.

## Flow
- owner at UTC+2 asks "What happened each day?"
- a deal created at 01:00 local on day D+1 (23:00 UTC on day D) is on D+1 in the window table and on D in the wallet table
- window table and wallet table give different counts per day for the same question

## Expected impact
The two tables under one answer agree line for line. Could break: every BookQuery consumer if a field is added (contract).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - deals grouped on the same day by both tables
Before: probe (large world, TZ offset -120): 37 of 500 deals have dayKey != UTC date
After: predicted 0 of 500; not built: crates/table-ledger is outside this round and BookQuery is a contract
Method: probe - vitest over the large mock world comparing dayKey with toISOString().slice(0,10)
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: direction.test.ts-style test: a deal at 00:30 local in a UTC+2 calendar; window day line and mock book_query day line must name the same day (mock mirrors book.rs)

title: Align the window's recovered money with the wallet's one predicate
body:
## Summary
The window counts recovered money as any settled sandbox rescue or invoice; the wallet counts only verified rescue receipts, so the two Recovered columns under one answer can differ.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/model.ts:205 isRecovered = kind rescue|invoice && isSettled && sandbox. crates/table-ledger/src/rescue.rs:100 COUNTED (the "one place it is written") = kind rescue, state RECEIPTED|RECONCILED, receipt_evidence paypal_verified, a paypal rescue case, a verified receipt and a confirmed invoice-send. The window also feeds the bars (where.ts flowOf). Within the client, the typed "recovered" chip filters kinds [rescue] (understand.ts:67) while the preset lens filters [rescue, invoice] (model.ts:151). The mock mirrors the client rule, so the large world agrees (204179 both) and hides the gap. Fixed: one rule - narrow isRecovered to what the client can see of COUNTED (kind rescue, RECEIPTED|RECONCILED, sandbox) and show the wallet's figure as the authority; align the chip and the lens on one kind set.

## Flow
- a CAPTURED (not yet RECEIPTED) sandbox rescue: window counts it recovered, wallet does not
- a settled sandbox invoice-kind deal: window counts it, wallet never does
- the "How much did rescues bring back?" answer shows two different Recovered figures

## Expected impact
The owner sees one recovered figure, the wallet's rule. Could break: the bars' rescue paid segment (flowOf).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - window and wallet Recovered agree on the same deals
Before: simulation: 2 of 3 walked cases disagree (CAPTURED rescue, settled invoice); large mock world agrees only because the mock mirrors the client
After: predicted 0 of 3 disagree
Method: simulation - the instrument needs a client fixture mirroring a book.rs recovered test; the mock cannot show the gap
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: model.test.ts: deals {rescue CAPTURED sandbox, invoice RECEIPTED sandbox, rescue RECEIPTED sandbox}; assert aggregate().recovered counts only the last, mirroring book.rs query_bounds_and_recovered_metric_exclude_replay

title: Give "Stopped" one set: the tile, the answer line and the stopped question
body:
## Summary
"Stopped" names two sets in the Book: the tile and answer line count 9 states (refunds, disputes and failures included), the "What was stopped" question and typed "stopped" filter 6, from two hand-copied lists.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/model.ts:29-38 bucketOf puts REFUNDED, DISPUTED and FAILED in "stopped" (tile note "never paid, or paid back", lib/words/book.ts BOOK.answer.stopped "stopped or paid back"). model.ts:133 STOPPED and understand.ts:58 STOPPED (identical copies) list only REFUSED, VOIDED, AUTO_VOIDED, WITHDRAWN, EXPIRED, MISMATCH. So the Stopped tile and the stopped question count different deals. Fixed: one exported list derived from bucketOf (or one shared constant both files import), and the chip title and tile note saying the same thing; which set "stopped" means is the owner's word to pick.

## Flow
- Book ledger: Stopped tile counts bucket stopped
- Ask: "What was stopped, and why?" filters STOPPED
- large world: tile 148 deals, question 147

## Expected impact
The tile and the question it invites agree. Could break: walletSumsApart for the new list (stays one bucket).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one concept, one set
Before: probe (large world): bucket stopped 148 vs stopped lens 147; 2 hand copies of STOPPED
After: predicted 148 vs 148 (or both 147 if paid-back is excluded), 1 list
Method: probe - vitest over the large mock world; not built because the choice of set is a wording decision
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: model.test.ts: on a deal per state, LENSES.stopped rows === deals with bucketOf stopped; seed by re-adding a hand list

title: Keep "Go to a day" reading when a scroll page is already out
body:
## Summary
The record's "Go to a day" stops silently when a scroll-triggered page read is in flight, then filters to that day and can show "Nothing on record yet." for a day it never reached.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/book/Record.tsx page() returns undefined while busy (busy.current), and goDay breaks its loop on undefined; jumping ends, the day filter (shown = rows with at < day end) keeps only rows older than the day, which were never read, so the list is empty and its empty state claims nothing is on record. Fixed: goDay waits for the in-flight page (or retries once it settles) and, if it stops short, says the day was not reached.

## Flow
- scroll the record near its end (a page read starts)
- pick a date in "Go to a day" before it lands
- goDay -> page() undefined -> break -> filtered list empty -> "Nothing on record yet."

## Expected impact
A jump to an old day lands or says it could not. Could break: the bounded MAX_JUMP_PAGES loop.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a jump reaches its day or says it did not
Before: simulation: 1 walked race ends with an empty list and a false empty-state claim
After: predicted the jump continues after the in-flight page
Method: simulation - needs a harness backend with a delayed audit_page; not built in this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: book.test.tsx: harness backend delaying audit_page; click "Read older steps", then set the date field to a day older than the first page; assert a second page was read and the list is not the empty state

title: Count text filter length in bytes as book.rs does
body:
## Summary
rules.ts checks text filter values by UTF-16 length, book.rs bound() by UTF-8 bytes.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/rules.ts (text values 1 to 256) vs crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:76-79 s.len() <= 256. The only text values the reader builds are kinds, states and counterparty key ids, all ASCII, where the two lengths are equal.

## Flow
- enumerate the values understand.ts compose() can emit

## Expected impact
None reachable.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mirror refuses what Rust refuses
Before: 0 of the reachable values differ (ASCII kinds, states, key ids)
After: 0 of 0
Method: probe - enumeration of compose() outputs
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence:
rules.ts: typeof v !== 'string' || !v.length || v.length > 256
book.rs:78: .filter(|s| !s.is_empty() && s.len() <= 256)
